description: Three measured surfaces: the FILTER (WHERE cond) aggregate clause does not exist in Snowflake - every use is a syntax error (plain, grouped, in expressions, HAVING, with OVER) while the portable spellings (CASE-wrapped arguments, COUNT_IF) work and FILTER stays a plain identifier; FLOAT-to-VARCHAR renders with 10 significant digits (C %.10g, trailing zeros stripped - 0.8999999762, not Java's shortest round-trip), short and integral doubles keeping their short forms, so a SHA2 over the stringified float matches Snowflake's record-id recipe; and hex binary literals x'A1B2' / X'a1b2' carry the real BINARY value (uppercase hex display), equal to TO_BINARY of the same hex and insertable into BINARY columns. Converted 1:1 from expressions/FilterClauseAggregateTest + expressions/FloatToVarcharTest + expressions/HexBinaryLiteralTest (now retired).

steps.sql: CREATE TABLE ft (a INTEGER, b INTEGER, c INTEGER, g INTEGER)
SELECT SUM(a) FILTER(WHERE c > 0) FROM ft
SELECT COUNT(a) FILTER(WHERE c > 0) FROM ft
SELECT g, SUM(a) FILTER(WHERE c > 0) FROM ft GROUP BY g ORDER BY g
SELECT MIN_BY(a, b) FILTER(WHERE c = 2) FROM ft
SELECT SUM(a) FILTER(WHERE c > 0) + 1 FROM ft
SELECT g FROM ft GROUP BY g HAVING SUM(a) FILTER(WHERE c > 0) > 5
CREATE TABLE ft (a INTEGER, b INTEGER, c INTEGER, g INTEGER)
SELECT SUM(a) FILTER(WHERE c > 0) OVER (PARTITION BY g) FROM ft
CREATE TABLE ft (a INTEGER, b INTEGER, c INTEGER, g INTEGER)
SELECT SUM(CASE WHEN c > 0 THEN a END) FROM ft
